title: Standard MLA, six schedules
formula: out = softmax([q_nope|q_rope] @ [k_nope|k_rope]^T * scale) @ v over a single-head KV cache, Dn=512 or 448, Dr=64, FP16 or BF16, BSND and BNSD
study_for: Six schedules that all preserve the original 4-D ABI: no host packing, no GM workspace, no extra launch, no integer rescaling. That constraint is what shapes all six. `serial_nd` is the deliberately simple correctness baseline; `prefill_resident` holds one KV tile to avoid repeated online-state updates; `decode_preload` and `online_prefetch` are the M128 pipelines; `online_paired` groups core intervals by even item ceilings; `decode_splitkv` is the one that breaks the no-workspace rule on purpose.

`decode_splitkv` is the one to read for a cross-core merge: FP32 partials into private GM workspace, an all-Vector barrier, then a stable log-sum-exp merge in the SAME kernel, with producer M64 groups and merge row groups distributed independently. The inputs stay read-only throughout.

`serial_nd` documents a padding obligation that is easy to miss: eight logical query heads share one physical M16 cube tile, so every Q and P row that M16 reads has to be initialised — including the rows belonging to the vector participant that does no work.

The four `serial_*` cases are controls, not extra coverage. Each runs `serial_nd` at exactly the shape of a teaching case, so when an optimised schedule disagrees with the oracle you can tell whether the shape or the schedule is at fault. Use `--variant` to run one schedule across every case that selects it.

MLA's KV cache has one head: `k_nope`, `k_rope` and `v` carry 1 where the query carries Nq, and `v` holds `k_nope`'s own values in separate storage. That absorbed-V form is the layout, not an accident of the input generator.
do_not_copy_when: You are taking `serial_nd` as a performance model. It is a correctness baseline and says so; the other five exist because it is not fast.
You need causal positions from a host-side table. These schedules recover the causal query position from each physical row instead, which is what lets them keep the 4-D ABI.

Your KV cache has more than one head. Every one of the six is built on each query head reading the same key; that is the difference between this and a5_mha_fp16_bf16, which is the demo to read for independent per-head K and V.
